The duplicated `Subsingleton`↔`IsZero` conversion is real. But each copy is a one-term, three-step application of existing API, and the mathematical content is trivial. The rubric excludes short calculations and thin wrappers around existing API. A lemma `GradedModuleCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton`, parallel to the ModuleCat one, could still be a reasonable API addition under a different rubric (missing basic API). claims.reason:
The repeated pattern is `(IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero X).2 (hom_ext (LinearMap.ext fun _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _))`. That is a one-line composition of three existing lemmas, the same shape as Mathlib's one-line `ModuleCat.isZero_of_subsingleton`. It is routine unfolding of the definition of a zero object, not nontrivial mathematical reasoning, so it falls under the rubric's exclusions for short calculations and thin wrappers over existing API.

The cited sites are also not uniform. (1) The `Nontrivial Y` block (lines 59–63) never shows `IsZero Y`. It shows `i = 0` from `Subsingleton Y`, using `map_zero` rewrites. That is a different argument, and it needs `hi₀ : i ≠ 0`. I confirmed the signature of `exists_mono_ne_zero_not_isIso_of_not_simple` gives `f ≠ 0`. (2) The two ProjectiveBasis copies work on full-subcategory objects and need an extra `ObjectProperty.hom_ext` layer. The proposed lemma would not apply to them directly. (3) The SimpleBasis line-84 `hM` proves the converse implication, from a nonzero element to `¬IsZero`, so it is not a duplicate of the construction. (4) `isZero_finiteZero` in CartanMap/Basic.lean uses `PUnit`, with an unfolded `apply` chain.

The only exact duplicate is the `Q` block here, plus the SimpleBasis line-120 copy and the ProjectiveBasis copies up to the subcategory wrapper. These are tiny, so extracting a lemma would add API for little gain. This may be worthwhile under an API-completeness rubric, but it does not satisfy the repeated-proof-machinery rubric.
